sources.title: NGSS MS-LS1-4: Use argument based on empirical evidence and scientific reasoning to support an explanation for how characteristic animal behaviors and specialized plant structures affect the probability of successful reproduction of animals and plants respectively
OpenStax Biology 2e, 26.4 The Role of Seed Plants
OpenStax Biology 2e, 26.1 Evolution of Seed Plants

printed.text: Carried by a bee or the wind

steps.title: Stamen
steps.instruction: Trace the stamen: the anther on its stalk.

note.text: The anther at the top of the stamen makes pollen. Pollen grains carry the plant's sperm.

steps.title: Carpel
steps.instruction: Trace the carpel: stigma, style and ovary.

note.text: The sticky stigma on top traps pollen. A stalk, the style, leads down to the ovary at the bottom.

steps.title: Ovules
steps.instruction: Trace the three ovules inside the ovary.

note.text: Each ovule holds an egg cell. Each ovule can become a seed.

steps.title: Pollination
steps.instruction: Draw pollen moving from the anther to the stigma.

note.text: Pollination is pollen landing on a stigma. Insects, birds, wind or water carry it, often from another flower.

steps.title: Pollen tube
steps.instruction: Draw the pollen tube growing down the style.

note.text: The pollen grain grows a tube down through the style to an ovule. The sperm travel down inside it.
note.remember: Pollen tube: carries sperm to the egg.

steps.title: Pollen grain
steps.instruction: Dab the pollen grain on the stigma.

note.text: When a sperm joins the egg in the ovule, that's fertilization. The ovule then grows into a seed.
Bright petals, scent and sweet nectar draw in animals. As they feed, pollen dusts their bodies.

steps.title: From pollen to seed
items: Pollen tube grows down the style
steps.why: Pollen is carried to the stigma, grows a tube to the ovule, and fertilization turns the ovule into a seed.

steps.title: Name the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the name for each numbered part.

mistakes.Anther: The anther makes pollen. The sticky tip that catches it is the stigma.

targets.role: The pollen tube grows down it.

mistakes.Ovary: The ovary is the whole chamber. Each small oval inside it is an ovule.

steps.title: Argue
steps.question: How do bright petals and sweet nectar help a plant reproduce?

options.text: They attract animals that carry pollen between flowers, so more ovules get fertilized
options.feedback: Yes. More pollinator visits mean more pollen reaches stigmas, so the plant is likelier to make seeds.

options.text: They make food for the seeds
options.feedback: Petals don't feed seeds. They attract the animals that carry pollen.
They do the opposite: they attract the pollinators the plant needs.
The anthers make pollen. Petals attract animals that carry it.

steps.title: Fruit
steps.question: After the ovules become seeds, what does the ovary around them become?

options.feedback: Right. The ovary wall thickens into a fruit that protects the seeds and helps spread them.
The ovary becomes the fruit. New flowers grow from new buds.
Pollen comes from anthers. The ovary becomes the fruit.
Roots grow from a seed's embryo after it sprouts. The ovary becomes the fruit.
